name: slatwall-ts
description: Extracted Slatwall Catalog slice - Product, Sku, Brand, Option and the Google product-feed adapter - as a strict-mode TypeScript AWS Lambda service over the existing MySQL Sw* schema.
//dependencyInventory: ELEVEN DEV DEPENDENCIES ARE DECLARED WHERE THE PLAN'S INVENTORY LISTS TEN. The eleventh is
ts-node 10.9.2, and it is recorded here rather than left as a silent difference between the
WHY IT IS PRESENT: AAP 0.4.1.2 and the target tree in AAP 0.3.1 both require the test
configuration to be jest.config.ts - a TypeScript file. jest-config loads a .ts config by
dynamically importing ts-node (node_modules/jest-config/build/index.js) and declares it as an
OPTIONAL PEER dependency, ts-node >=9.0.0. Node 20 cannot strip types on its own, so on this
pinned runtime the AAP-mandated jest.config.ts is unloadable without it and `npm test` fails
WHY IT IS NOT REMOVED: the alternative is renaming jest.config.ts to .js or .cjs, which would
restore the count of ten by violating two explicit AAP rows. Keeping the AAP-mandated filename
and documenting the consequence is the lesser deviation, and it is the one recorded here.
IT IS DEV-ONLY AND NEVER SHIPPED: build/esbuild.mjs bundles only src/handlers/**, ts-node is
reachable from no source file, and the emitted artifacts require nothing but mysql2/promise and
two node: built-ins. The pin is exact, like every other row.
REMOVAL TRIGGER: a runtime that strips TypeScript types natively, or a jest-config release that
loads a .ts config without ts-node. Either makes this row unnecessary; neither is available on
the pinned nodejs20 line, so retargeting the runtime is the event that should re-examine it.
//securityRemediation: The overrides block below is a SECURITY REMEDIATION, not a preference, and it is not authorised
by any AAP dependency row - AAP 0.5.2 describes direct dependencies and an engines field only.
It is recorded here, in full, so a reviewer auditing the manifest finds the reasoning beside the
block rather than having to reconstruct it.
ADVISORY: GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg / CVE-2026-14257, unbounded brace expansion in brace-expansion,
reachable transitively through the Jest toolchain only (dev-time; nothing here is bundled).
WHAT IS REPLACED: minimatch is pinned to 10.2.6, replacing the 1.x/2.x/3.x copies the resolved
graph would otherwise install; test-exclude is pinned to 7.0.2, replacing its 6.x range. Both
are the two CONSUMERS of brace-expansion inside that toolchain.
REJECTED ALTERNATIVES: NEVER add brace-expansion itself - 5.x is ESM with named exports while
minimatch 1/2/3 require the default-export expand function, so that override fails at runtime
with "expand is not a function". And glob is not pinned, because glob 13 is only reachable by
replacing the glob that jest's own reporters require, whereas pinning minimatch fixes the leaf
consumer both vulnerable paths share and leaves jest's resolved graph intact.
VERIFICATION: npm ci exit 0 with 398 packages, npm audit 0 vulnerabilities, npm install
--package-lock-only produces no lockfile change, and the full suite is green. Re-verified after
the QA remediation that added this note.
REMOVAL TRIGGER: when jest and its reporters resolve a brace-expansion release that carries the
fix without an override, drop both pins and re-run npm ci plus npm audit to confirm the graph is
clean on its own. Until then removing them reintroduces the advisory.
This note IS the rationale - it is deliberately kept here rather than in jest.config.ts, because
a reader auditing the overrides reads this file, and package.json admits no comment syntax other
than a '//' member.
